gap: No result ChatGPT got states that Thinkware's side-camera setup (ARC 800 + Multiplexer Box) records the side cameras and the rear camera together as one merged 1920 × 1080 file. In that setup each side view gets at most about 960 × 540 pixels (about 7.4 px per degree), while the Botslab G980H records each side camera as its own 1080p channel (about 16 px per degree), roughly 4× the pixels per side view.
standout_why: I compared this against DashCamTalk's best-dash-cams page, which ChatGPT cited and which I opened. It lists no model with left or right cameras, and its only 4-channel pick, the Vantrue N5S, uses its extra two cameras inside the cabin. I also checked CarAudioRadar's 'left and right cameras' list, the top organic result in chat 2. It warns that '4K front' does not mean every feed is 4K, but it never mentions Thinkware or the multiplexer's merged file and gives no pixel-per-view or pixel-per-degree figure. Thinkware's own help article, which ChatGPT cited, says the feeds are 'merged and sent to the dash cam' through the rear-camera port, but it never works out what each view gets. ChatGPT then called the Thinkware setup 'Best premium setup' with '1080p side cameras', so the answer the shopper saw implies the opposite of this finding. I could not open Car and Driver (the fetch tool is blocked on that site), so I can't rule out that it covers this, and I scored 2, not 3.
decides: This supports the Botslab G980H 4-Camera as the pick for side footage you can actually read: each side camera records 1920 × 1080 into its own channel at 120°. Thinkware's 4-view setup costs $539.96 at Thinkware's US store (read 2026-11-21) and shares one 1080p frame between the rear and both side cameras. It still wins one segment honestly: its side cameras mount outside the glass and are rated IP68, so window tint and reflections don't get in the way. The Botslab and Rexing side lenses film through the side windows. The Vantrue N5S belongs off this page, because none of its four cameras faces the left or right side.
candidates: Thinkware ARC 800 + Multiplexer Box + 2× Exterior Side View Camera

findings.label: Channels and what each camera sees
findings.value: 4 channels: front, left, right, rear. Resolution is listed as 3K + 1080P + 1080P + 1080P
findings.note: The page gives 'Video Resolution: 3K+1080P+1080P+1080P' and 'Angle of View: 170+120+120+150' in the order Front/Left/Right/Rear. It does not name a sensor or give a frame rate.

findings.label: Side camera pixels per degree (derived)
findings.note: 1920 px ÷ 120° = 16.0 px/°. Botslab doesn't say whether the 120° is diagonal or horizontal. If it is diagonal, as Thinkware's figure is, the two are directly comparable.

findings.label: Recorded pixels per side view (derived)
findings.note: 1920 × 1080 = 2,073,600. Each side camera is its own 1080P channel in the 4-channel mode.

findings.label: Parking mode, storage, heat, GPS
findings.value: Parking mode needs a hardwire kit, which is not included. microSD up to 512 GB, 128 GB card included. Supercapacitor rated -20 °C to 70 °C. Built-in GPS and Wi-Fi.
findings.note: The page says '24/7 Parking Mode: ✓ (Hard wire kit needed)' and 'Hard Wire Kit: Not Included'. I did not read a price for the hardwire kit.

findings.product: Thinkware ARC 800 + Multiplexer Box + 2× Exterior Side View Camera
findings.label: How the multiplexer records the extra cameras
findings.value: All add-on cameras go into one file, through the dash cam's rear-camera port, as a single composite 1920 × 1080 stream at 30 fps
findings.note: The store page lists up to four analog Full HD cameras (5 channels in total), a composite output of 1920 × 1080 at 30 fps, and a 7.5 m ARC rear-camera cable in the box. Thinkware's multi-channel page (https://thinkwarestore.com/multi-channel/, read 2026-11-21) says 'The recordings from additional cameras cannot be saved separately, they will be saved in one file only.' The help article (https://support.thinkware.com/hc/en-us/articles/6987667899539-How-to-Install-the-Multiplexer-box, read 2026-11-21) says the feeds are 'merged and sent to the dash cam' through the V-out cable to the rearview camera port, and placed 'clockwise starting from the top left' by port number.

findings.product: Thinkware ARC 800 + Multiplexer Box + 2× Exterior Side View Camera
findings.label: Recorded pixels per side view, rear + 2 sides merged (derived)
findings.source_title: How to Install the Multiplexer box – Thinkware Help Center
findings.note: 1920 × 1080 ÷ 4 tiles = 960 × 540 = 518,400 px. The four-tile layout comes from the help article's top-left-clockwise port placement. Thinkware does not print 960 × 540 itself. Compared with the Botslab: 2,073,600 ÷ 518,400 = 4×.

findings.product: Thinkware ARC 800 + Multiplexer Box + 2× Exterior Side View Camera
findings.label: Side camera pixels per degree, merged (derived)
findings.source_title: Exterior Side View Cameras (Pack of 2), Thinkware Store
findings.note: 960 px ÷ 129° = 7.4 px/°. The side camera itself is 1920 × 1080 at 30 fps, 129° diagonal, 2.12 MP, IP68. Unmerged it would be 1920 ÷ 129 = 14.9 px/°, but that needs the side camera to take the rear port with no multiplexer, which leaves no rear camera.

findings.product: Thinkware ARC 800 + Multiplexer Box + 2× Exterior Side View Camera
findings.label: Price of the 4-view setup at Thinkware's US store (derived)
findings.note: $279.99 for the ARC 800 Front & Rear (sale, regular $329.99) + $99.99 for the Multiplexer Box + $159.98 for the side-camera 2-pack = $539.96. The three prices were read on their own Thinkware Store pages on 2026-11-21. The side-camera page's compatibility list (U1000 Plus, Q850, Q200, F200 PRO, F790, X800, X700) leaves out the ARC 800. The Multiplexer Box page and the help article do list the ARC 800.

findings.label: Front and rear cameras, parking, storage
findings.value: Front 4K at 30 fps or 2K at 60 fps, Sony STARVIS 2 IMX678, 146° diagonal. Rear 1080p at 30 fps, 125°. microSD up to 512 GB, 32 GB card included. Hardwiring cable included for parking mode. GPS built in.
findings.note: Once the multiplexer is fitted, the rear camera becomes one of the merged tiles.

findings.label: Price at Target
findings.note: Target says 'All around 1080p'. The left and right cameras have IR lights and can turn to face the cabin. Parking mode needs Rexing's type-C smart hardwire kit. The page contradicts itself on power backup: the staff Q&A says supercapacitor, the spec table says lithium-ion. Without a field of view, I could not work out its px/°.

findings.label: Which way its cameras face
findings.value: Front, rear, interior, interior rear. No left or right exterior camera.
findings.note: This matches our own record for the product (front, front cabin, rear cabin, rear). It belongs off a side-camera page.
